title: Forgetting a condensed profinite-group action creates filtered colimits
statement:
Let $R$ be a commutative condensed ring on the small site $P$ of profinite sets with finite jointly surjective coverings [sk-def-sfb-condensed-ring, def-weil-size-convention], and let $\operatorname{Mod}_R$ be its category of internal $R$-modules [sk-def-sfb-module-objects]. Let $J$ be a compact Hausdorff totally disconnected topological group, and let $\mathcal A_J(R)$ be internal $R$-modules with $R(S)$-linear actions of $\underline J(S)=C(S,J)$, natural in profinite parameters $S$, and equivariant maps [def-sfb-condensed-action-module]. Let $I$ be a small filtered category (nonempty, and every finite diagram has a cocone) and $N:I\to\mathcal A_J(R)$, $i\mapsto N_i$, a diagram [def-weil-pbc-category-colimit].

Then the colimit $L$ of the underlying diagram in $\operatorname{Mod}_R$ has sections $L(S)=\operatorname{colim}_iN_i(S)$ for every profinite $S$, with coprojections $\iota_i:N_i\to L$ sending $m$ to its class $[m]$. The formula $g[m]=[gm]$, for $g\in C(S,J)$ and $m\in N_i(S)$, is well defined and makes $L$ an object of $\mathcal A_J(R)$; every $\iota_i$ is equivariant. For every cocone $(\lambda_i:N_i\to M)_{i\in I}$ of equivariant maps to an object $M$ of $\mathcal A_J(R)$, the unique $R$-linear map $\lambda:L\to M$ with $\lambda\circ\iota_i=\lambda_i$ is equivariant. Hence $(L,(\iota_i))$ is a colimit of $N$ in $\mathcal A_J(R)$, and the forgetful functor $\mathcal A_J(R)\to\operatorname{Mod}_R$ creates this filtered colimit. All sites, parameters and indexing categories are in the compatible universes fixed above.

proof.text: Use the internal/sectionwise module equivalence to obtain a colimit of the underlying internal module diagram, and the module-sheaf forgetful-colimit theorem to obtain its abelian-sheaf colimit. Prove directly that the underlying abelian presheaf colimit is a sheaf: forgetting to sets preserves this filtered colimit, and for each finite effective epimorphic family the finite-presieve filtered-colimit lemma preserves the sheaf condition. Mathlib isSheaf_coherent identifies these families as a sheaf test for the coherent profinite topology. Thus sheaf inclusion creates this colimit. Evaluation gives an abelian-group colimit; forgetting scalars reflects colimits, so the original section-module cocones are colimits as well. This argument uses the universe-general finite-presieve sublemma of the previously approved finite-cover section theorem, whose SmallCategory site signature does not directly fit Profinite.

proof.text: For each profinite S and g in C(S,J), the maps iota_i composed with the linear action of g form a module cocone: equivariance of transition maps and the underlying cocone equation prove naturality. Descend this cocone through the section-module colimit to a linear endomorphism a_g. The colimit factorization equation gives a_g(iota_i(m)) = iota_i(gm). Every section has a representative, so the identity and multiplication laws follow from the corresponding stage action laws. The same representative formula, naturality of the underlying coprojections, and naturality of each stage action prove restriction compatibility. This constructs the action on the actual underlying module colimit, and the coprojections become equivariant.

proof.text: For an equivariant cocone d and an underlying factor f, evaluate on a representative iota_i(m). The factorization equations and equivariance of d_i give f(g iota_i(m)) = g f(iota_i(m)), so f is equivariant. The underlying colimit descent therefore defines an action-category colimit descent, with factorization and uniqueness inherited by subtype extensionality. Finally forgetting actions reflects isomorphisms: the inverse of an underlying isomorphism is equivariant by applying that inverse to the original equivariance equation and canceling the two inverse identities. Apply createsColimitOfReflectsIso' to the constructed lift of the underlying colimit. This supplies CreatesColimit, including reflection and lifts of arbitrary underlying colimit cocones.
